contentObjective: I can convert measurement units using ratios and conversion factors.
languageObjective: I can explain my conversion using the words conversion factor, unit, equivalent, and ratio.

vocabulary.definition: Rename a measurement in a different unit without changing its amount.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresar una medida en una unidad diferente sin cambiar su cantidad.
vocabulary.cloze: Renaming a measurement in a different unit without changing the amount is to ___ it.

examples.why: The amount changed, not just the unit.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio that helps you change one unit into another.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que te ayuda a cambiar una unidad por otra.
vocabulary.visual: 1 foot = 12 inches, so the factor is 12
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio equal to 1 that relates two units, like 12 inches / 1 foot, is a ___.

examples.why: The ratio that trades one unit for another.
That is the amount being converted.

vocabulary.definition: A standard amount used to measure, like an inch or a liter.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cantidad estándar para medir, como una pulgada o un litro.
vocabulary.cloze: A standard amount used to measure, like a foot or a gram, is a ___.

examples.why: A standard amount you measure with.
That counts units; it is not one.

vocabulary.definition: Having the same value, just in different units.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tener el mismo valor, solo en unidades distintas.
vocabulary.cloze: Two measurements that name the same amount, like 1 foot and 12 inches, are ___.

examples.why: The same amount, named two ways.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A comparison of two quantities is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: The U.S. way of measuring, like inches, feet, and pounds.

vocabulary.cloze: Units like inches, feet, and pounds used mainly in the U.S. are ___.

examples.why: A foot is a customary unit of length.
A meter is a metric unit.

vocabulary.definition: A way of measuring by 10s, like meters, liters, and grams.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una forma de medir de 10 en 10, como metros, litros y gramos.
vocabulary.cloze: Units like meters, grams, and liters based on tens are ___.

examples.why: A gram is a metric unit of mass.
A pound is a customary unit.

vocabulary.visual: Cups of juice: 2, 4, 6 | Cups of water: 3, 6, 9

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Bridge Engineering
revealWordProblem.text: The Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables are each about 7,650 feet long. A supply company sells cable-protection wrap in spools measured in yards. How many yards of protective wrap does one full cable need? Show your work using a conversion factor.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 1 yard = 3 feet, so converting feet to the larger unit (yards) means dividing by the conversion factor: 7,650 ÷ 3 = 2,550 yards. One cable needs 2,550 yards of protective wrap.

questions.stem: How many inches are in 7 feet?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 7 by 12 (inches per foot).
There are 12 inches in every foot.
You multiplied by 8 feet. Re-read how many feet the question gives.
hints: The key fact: 1 foot = 12 inches. You have 7 feet and want inches.
Going from a BIGGER unit (feet) to a SMALLER unit (inches) means you multiply.
Set up 7 × 12 — seven groups of 12 inches.
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 pie = 12 pulgadas. Tienes 7 pies y quieres pulgadas.
Ir de una unidad MAYOR (pies) a una MENOR (pulgadas) significa que multiplicas.
Plantea 7 × 12: siete grupos de 12 pulgadas.

questions.stem: How many feet are in 3 yards?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 3 by 3 (feet per yard).
There are 3 feet in every yard.
Not quite. 1 yard = ___ feet.
hints: The key fact: 1 yard = 3 feet. You have 3 yards and want feet.
Big unit (yards) to small unit (feet) means multiply by the conversion factor 3.
Set up 3 × 3 — three yards, each worth 3 feet.
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 yarda = 3 pies. Tienes 3 yardas y quieres pies.
De unidad grande (yardas) a unidad pequeña (pies) significa multiplicar por el factor de conversión 3.
Plantea 3 × 3: tres yardas, cada una de 3 pies.

questions.stem: How many ounces are in 4 pounds?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 4 by 16 (ounces per pound).
There are 16 ounces in every pound.
Not quite. 1 pound = ___ ounces.
hints: The key fact: 1 pound = 16 ounces. You have 4 pounds and want ounces.
Pounds are bigger than ounces, so converting to ounces means multiplying by 16.
Set up 4 × 16. (Break it up: 4 × 10 = 40 and 4 × 6 = 24, then add.)
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 libra = 16 onzas. Tienes 4 libras y quieres onzas.
Las libras son mayores que las onzas, así que convertir a onzas significa multiplicar por 16.
Plantea 4 × 16. (Sepáralo: 4 × 10 = 40 y 4 × 6 = 24, y luego suma.)

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Convert Measurement Units is applying the conversion factor in the wrong direction — for example, converting 4 feet to inches by dividing (4 ÷ 12 = 0.33 inches) instead of multiplying (4 × 12 = 48 inches), or converting 80 ounces to pounds by multiplying (80 × 16 = 1,280 pounds) instead of dividing (80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds). Before you answer, ask: am I changing to a SMALLER unit (there will be MORE of them, so multiply) or a BIGGER unit (there will be FEWER of them, so divide)?

choiceFeedback: Divide 24 by 12 (inches per foot).
There are 12 inches in one foot.
That is the number of inches. Going from inches to feet means dividing.
hints: This one goes the OTHER direction: inches (small) to feet (big), so the number of units gets smaller.
Small unit to big unit means divide. Ask: how many groups of 12 inches fit in 24 inches?
Set up 24 ÷ 12.
hintsEs: Esta va en la dirección CONTRARIA: de pulgadas (pequeña) a pies (grande), así que el número de unidades se hace menor.
De unidad pequeña a unidad grande significa dividir. Pregunta: ¿cuántos grupos de 12 pulgadas caben en 24 pulgadas?
Plantea 24 ÷ 12.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.4) A ratio table shows (2, 6), (4, 12), and (6, 18). Which ordered pair comes next if the pattern continues?
level1.explanation: The pattern adds 2 to x and 6 to y each time. After (6, 18): x = 6+2 = 8, y = 18+6 = 24. The next point is (8, 24).
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The pattern adds 2 to x and 6 to y each time.
Your x-value follows the pattern, but y only moved up 4. Look at how much y grows from one row to the next.
This jumps two steps in x while y only takes one. Each row moves x and y forward together, so check the step size for both.
hints: Watch each coordinate separately: x goes 2, 4, 6, … and y goes 6, 12, 18, …
Find the jump in the x-values and the jump in the y-values, then apply both jumps to (6, 18).
The x-values climb by 2, so add 2 to the 6 first. Then find the y-jump from 6 → 12 → 18 and add it to 18.
level1.stemEs: Una tabla de razones muestra (2, 6), (4, 12) y (6, 18). ¿Cuál par ordenado sigue si el patrón continúa?
level1.explanationEs: El patrón suma 2 a x y 6 a y cada vez. Después de (6, 18): x = 6+2 = 8, y = 18+6 = 24. El siguiente punto es (8, 24).
hintsEs: Observa cada coordenada por separado: x va 2, 4, 6, … y y va 6, 12, 18, …
Halla el salto de los valores de x y el salto de los valores de y, y luego aplica ambos saltos a (6, 18).
Los valores de x suben de 2 en 2, así que suma 2 al 6 primero. Luego halla el salto de y de 6 → 12 → 18 y súmalo a 18.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.4) When you graph equivalent ratios, the points will always form what shape?
choices: A straight line through the origin
level1.explanation: Equivalent ratios are proportional, so their graph is always a straight line that passes through the origin (0, 0).
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
A zigzag would mean the ratio changes from point to point. Equivalent ratios grow by the same step every time, so the points stay in line.
A circle would bring the points back to where they started. Equivalent ratios keep climbing in one direction as x increases.
hints: Think about what happened when you plotted equivalent-ratio points earlier in this lesson.
Equivalent ratios grow steadily: every time x rises by the same amount, y rises by the same amount. What shape is steady growth?
Picture plotting (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6) and connecting them — and check whether (0, 0) would fit the pattern too.
level1.stemEs: Cuando graficas razones equivalentes, ¿qué forma tomarán siempre los puntos?
level1.explanationEs: Las razones equivalentes son proporcionales, así que su gráfica siempre es una línea recta que pasa por el origen (0, 0).
choicesEs: Una línea recta que pasa por el origen
hintsEs: Piensa en lo que pasó cuando graficaste puntos de razones equivalentes antes en esta lección.
Las razones equivalentes crecen de manera pareja: cada vez que x sube lo mismo, y sube lo mismo. ¿Qué forma tiene un crecimiento parejo?
Imagina graficar (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6) y unirlos, y revisa si (0, 0) también encajaría en el patrón.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.5) Chef A uses 2 cups of cheese for every 8 crackers. Chef B uses 3 cups of cheese for every 9 crackers. Who uses more cheese per cracker?
level1.explanation: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 cups per cracker. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 cups per cracker. Chef B uses more cheese per cracker.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Chef A: 2÷8 = ___ cups per cracker.
The two ratios do not reduce to the same value, so they are not equal. Divide each cheese amount by its cracker count and compare the results.
You have both amounts, so a comparison is possible. Turn each ratio into cheese per cracker and the answer appears.
hints: You can't compare 2 cups and 3 cups directly — the chefs use different numbers of crackers.
Find each chef's cheese for ONE cracker: divide cheese by crackers for each, then compare the two rates.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compare those two decimals to see who uses more per cracker.
level1.stemEs: El chef A usa 2 tazas de queso por cada 8 galletas saladas. El chef B usa 3 tazas de queso por cada 9 galletas saladas. ¿Quién usa más queso por galleta?
level1.explanationEs: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 tazas por galleta. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 tazas por galleta. El chef B usa más queso por galleta.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar 2 tazas y 3 tazas directamente: los chefs usan cantidades distintas de galletas.
Halla el queso de cada chef para UNA galleta: divide queso entre galletas en cada caso y luego compara las dos tasas.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compara esos dos decimales para ver quién usa más por galleta.

level1.explanation: Convert to the same denominator: 3:4 = 6:8. Since 6:8 > 5:8, the ratio 3:4 is greater.
choiceFeedback: Compare the ratios carefully — which one is greater?
Rewrite both ratios with the same second number before deciding. Scaling 3:4 so its second term is 8 makes the comparison direct.
Both ratios are exact numbers, so they can be compared. Scale one of them until the second terms match.
hints: The second numbers (4 and 8) don't match, so the ratios aren't ready to compare yet.
Rewrite the ratios with the same second number — 8 works nicely, since 4 × 2 = 8 — then compare the first numbers.
Scale 3:4 by 2: multiply both parts to get an out-of-8 ratio. Then compare its first number with the 5 in 5:8.
level1.explanationEs: Convierte a un denominador común: 3:4 = 6:8. Como 6:8 > 5:8, la razón 3:4 es mayor.
hintsEs: Los segundos números (4 y 8) no coinciden, así que las razones todavía no están listas para compararse.
Reescribe las razones con el mismo segundo número —el 8 funciona bien, porque 4 × 2 = 8— y luego compara los primeros números.
Escala 3:4 por 2: multiplica ambas partes para obtener una razón sobre 8. Luego compara su primer número con el 5 de 5:8.

level2.stem: A shelf is 30 inches long. How many feet and inches is that?
choiceFeedback: Divide by 12 and look for a remainder: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 R6.
Find how many complete feet fit, then how many inches left over.
18 inches is more than a foot, so this answer is not finished. Keep taking out groups of 12 inches until fewer than 12 remain.
hints: 30 inches is more than 2 feet (24 in) but less than 3 feet (36 in) — so the answer is 2 feet plus some leftover inches.
Divide by 12 to find whole feet; the REMAINDER stays as inches.
Compute 30 ÷ 12: it goes in 2 whole times using up 24 inches. Subtract 30 − 24 to find the leftover inches.
level2.stemEs: Un estante mide 30 pulgadas de largo. ¿A cuántos pies y pulgadas equivale?
level2.explanationEs: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 y sobran 6. Entonces 30 pulgadas = 2 pies 6 pulgadas.
hintsEs: 30 pulgadas es más de 2 pies (24 pulg) pero menos de 3 pies (36 pulg), así que la respuesta es 2 pies más unas pulgadas sobrantes.
Divide entre 12 para hallar los pies enteros; el RESIDUO se queda como pulgadas.
Calcula 30 ÷ 12: cabe 2 veces enteras usando 24 pulgadas. Resta 30 − 24 para hallar las pulgadas sobrantes.

level2.stem: Leg 1: The joystick rod is 3 feet long, but the parts catalog lists it in inches. How many inches is that? (1 ft = 12 in)
level2.explanation: Inches are smaller than feet, so multiply: 3 × 12 = 36 inches.
choiceFeedback: Multiply by 12 (inches per foot).
How many inches per foot?
Check the conversion factor: a foot is 12 inches, not 11. Multiply the number of feet by 12.
level2.stemEs: Tramo 1: La barra de la palanca de mando mide 3 pies de largo, pero el catálogo de piezas la lista en pulgadas. ¿A cuántas pulgadas equivale? (1 pie = 12 pulgadas)
level2.explanationEs: Las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que multiplica: 3 × 12 = 36 pulgadas.
hints: Converting to a smaller unit always produces a larger count of those units.
Decide whether to multiply or divide: inches are smaller than feet, so the number goes up.
Use the factor 1 ft = 12 in and set up 3 × 12. Finish that multiplication to get the length in inches.
hintsEs: Convertir a una unidad más pequeña siempre produce una cantidad mayor de esas unidades.
Decide si multiplicar o dividir: las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que el número aumenta.
Usa el factor 1 pie = 12 pulgadas y plantea 3 × 12. Termina esa multiplicación para obtener la longitud en pulgadas.

level2.stem: Leg 2: A power cable on the cabinet plan measures 2.5 kilometers across the whole arcade network. How many meters is that? (1 km = 1,000 m)
level2.explanation: Meters are smaller than kilometers, so multiply: 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500 meters.
choiceFeedback: Multiply by 1000.
1000 meters per kilometer.
That is a multiplication by 10,000 instead of 1,000. There are 1,000 meters in a kilometer, so the digits shift three places, not four.
level2.stemEs: Tramo 2: Un cable de energía en el plano del gabinete mide 2.5 kilómetros a lo largo de toda la red de la sala de juegos. ¿A cuántos metros equivale? (1 km = 1,000 m)
level2.explanationEs: Los metros son más pequeños que los kilómetros, así que multiplica: 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500 metros.
hints: A kilometer is much longer than a meter, so the number of meters will be much larger than 2.5.
Multiply by the conversion factor, because you are moving to a smaller unit.
Set up 2.5 × 1,000. Multiplying by 1,000 shifts the decimal point three places — move it and read the result.
hintsEs: Un kilómetro es mucho más largo que un metro, así que la cantidad de metros será mucho mayor que 2.5.
Multiplica por el factor de conversión, porque estás pasando a una unidad más pequeña.
Plantea 2.5 × 1,000. Multiplicar por 1,000 mueve el punto decimal tres lugares: muévelo y lee el resultado.

level2.stem: Leg 3: The coin box weighs 5 pounds, but the shipping label needs the weight in ounces. How many ounces is that? (1 lb = 16 oz)
level2.explanation: Ounces are smaller than pounds, so multiply: 5 × 16 = 80 ounces.
choiceFeedback: Multiply by 16 (ounces per pound).
How many ounces per pound?
That is the number of ounces in a single pound. The box weighs 5 pounds, so the conversion factor still has to be applied to all of them.
level2.stemEs: Tramo 3: La caja de monedas pesa 5 libras, pero la etiqueta de envío necesita el peso en onzas. ¿A cuántas onzas equivale? (1 libra = 16 onzas)
level2.explanationEs: Las onzas son más pequeñas que las libras, así que multiplica: 5 × 16 = 80 onzas.
hints: Ounces are smaller than pounds, so 5 pounds turns into many more ounces.
Multiply the number of pounds by the number of ounces in one pound.
Write 5 × 16 and finish it. Breaking it up helps: 5 × 10 plus 5 × 6.
hintsEs: Las onzas son más pequeñas que las libras, así que 5 libras se convierten en muchas más onzas.
Multiplica la cantidad de libras por la cantidad de onzas que tiene una libra.
Escribe 5 × 16 y termínalo. Separarlo ayuda: 5 × 10 más 5 × 6.

level2.prompt: A recipe says you need 5 feet of ribbon, but the store only sells ribbon in inches. Another recipe says you need 2 yards of fabric, but your ruler measures in feet. Convert both measurements and explain the steps you used. Which conversion factor did you use each time?
level2.sentenceFrame: 5 feet = ___ inches because ___. 2 yards = ___ feet because ___. The conversion factors I used were ___.
level2.hint: First convert 5 feet to inches, then compare that total to the store's ribbon-selling unit.
hints: There are two separate conversions: 5 feet → inches, and 2 yards → feet. Each uses a different conversion factor.
Both go from a bigger unit to a smaller unit, so both are multiplication. Name the factor you use each time.
Start the ribbon: 5 × 12, since every foot holds 12 inches. Then the fabric: 2 × 3, since every yard holds 3 feet.
level2.explanation: Both conversions go from a bigger unit to a smaller one, so both multiply. Using 12 inches per foot, 5 × 12 = 60 inches of ribbon; using 3 feet per yard, 2 × 3 = 6 feet of fabric. Naming the conversion factor each time is what explains why both numbers grew.
level2.explanationEs: Las dos conversiones van de una unidad más grande a una más pequeña, así que ambas se multiplican. Con 12 pulgadas por pie, 5 × 12 = 60 pulgadas de cinta; con 3 pies por yarda, 2 × 3 = 6 pies de tela. Nombrar el factor de conversión cada vez es lo que explica por qué los dos números crecieron.
level2.promptEs: Una receta dice que necesitas 5 pies de listón, pero la tienda solo vende listón en pulgadas. Otra receta dice que necesitas 2 yardas de tela, pero tu regla mide en pies. Convierte las dos medidas y explica los pasos que usaste. ¿Qué factor de conversión usaste en cada caso?
hintsEs: Hay dos conversiones distintas: 5 pies → pulgadas y 2 yardas → pies. Cada una usa un factor de conversión diferente.
Ambas van de una unidad mayor a una menor, así que ambas son multiplicación. Nombra el factor que usas cada vez.
Empieza con el listón: 5 × 12, porque cada pie tiene 12 pulgadas. Luego la tela: 2 × 3, porque cada yarda tiene 3 pies.

level3.stem: Final Leg: The finished cabinet ships in a crate holding 8 quarts of packing gel, but the supplier sells gel by the gallon. How many gallons is that? (4 qt = 1 gal)
level3.explanation: Gallons are bigger than quarts, so divide: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 gallons.
choiceFeedback: Divide by 4 (quarts per gallon).
4 quarts per gallon.
That looks like 8 + 4 rather than a conversion. Quarts are smaller than gallons, so the number of gallons has to come out smaller than 8.
level3.stemEs: Tramo final: El gabinete terminado se envía en una caja con 8 cuartos de galón de gel de embalaje, pero el proveedor vende el gel por galón. ¿A cuántos galones equivale? (4 cuartos = 1 galón)
level3.explanationEs: Los galones son más grandes que los cuartos, así que divide: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 galones.
hints: Gallons are larger than quarts, so the number of gallons will be smaller than 8.
Moving to a larger unit means dividing by the conversion factor.
Set up 8 ÷ 4 using 4 qt = 1 gal, and finish the division.
hintsEs: Los galones son más grandes que los cuartos, así que la cantidad de galones será menor que 8.
Pasar a una unidad más grande significa dividir entre el factor de conversión.
Plantea 8 ÷ 4 usando 4 cuartos = 1 galón y termina la división.
